html:
Oyu Tolgoi, "Turquoise Hill", is a huge copper and gold mine in the Gobi Desert of southern Mongolia, about 80 kilometres from the Chinese border. Geologists found the main deposit in 2001.

The Canadian company Ivanhoe Mines made the discovery and later sold control to the Anglo-Australian giant Rio Tinto. In 2009 the Mongolian government signed a deal taking a share of about a third. Open pit mining began in 2013. The much larger underground mine, which digs out ore from far below, started production in 2023.

The mine is one of the largest investments ever made in Mongolia, and copper became its leading export, nearly all of it sold to China. Its income helped Mongolia's economy grow, but the deal caused long political fights over who should get the profits, and worries over water in the dry Gobi and over the herders who live there. It is a sign of how Mongolia moved from herding toward mining after the democratic revolution of 1990.
